Empirical Research Plan: Long-Run Effects of Chicago’s Double-Dose Algebra Policy

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
Strategy: Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (FRD)

Justification
• Assignment to double-dose algebra was based on a deterministic rule—8th-grade ITBS math score < 50th national percentile.  
• Compliance was high in the two cohorts we study (2003 and 2004) but not literally 100 %; hence the discontinuity is in the probability of treatment, not treatment status itself → fuzzy RD.  
• The rich administrative panel allows us to trace outcomes up to college enrollment for cohorts whose treatment status is fixed at course entry, making the RD estimand interpretable as the local average treatment effect (LATE) for compliers around the cutoff.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control

Treatment Variable (DD_i)  
DD_i = 1 if student i took two periods of 9th-grade algebra (regular + support class) in 2003 or 2004; 0 otherwise.

Instrument (Z_i)  
Z_i = 1 if student’s ITBS math percentile < 50; 0 if ≥ 50.

Control Group  
Students with ITBS math ≥ 50 who therefore took a single algebra period.

Running Variable  
R_i = centered ITBS math percentile score (R_i = percentile – 50).  
Cutoff at R_i = 0.

Treatment Timing  
Treatment occurs entirely in 9th grade (school year 2003-04 or 2004-05). Outcomes are followed through 11th-grade tests, graduation, and college entry.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions

A1. Continuity of Potential Outcomes at the Cutoff  
Absent treatment, mean potential outcomes vary smoothly in ITBS math score. This is plausible because the 50th percentile is arbitrary from families’ perspective and schools had no incentive to prepare specifically for it.

A2. No Precise Manipulation of the Running Variable  
Students could not strategically alter official ITBS scores taken in 8th grade. We will test for discontinuities in the density of scores (McCrary test) and in predetermined covariates.

A3. First-Stage Discontinuity & Monotonicity  
Probability of double-dose jumps up at the cutoff and there are no “defiers.” Scheduling constraints might prevent some below-cutoff students from being treated, but no above-cutoff student is forced into double-dose.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA) Locally  
Peer-composition spillovers are part of the treatment bundle; the RD contrast captures their combined effect. Cross-cell contamination across the cutoff is minimal within the narrow bandwidth.

A5. Local Common Trends for Long-Run Outcomes  
Because treatment is completed in 9th grade, later shocks should not differentially affect just-below vs. just-above cutoff students except through treatment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Principal Threats & Mitigations

T1. Manipulation or Heaping of ITBS Scores  
• McCrary density test.  
• Visual inspection of score histogram.  
• If manipulation detected, narrow bandwidths or use robust bias-corrected RD methods.

T2. Differential Attrition / Mobility  
• Compare exit rates from CPS and national clearinghouse coverage by side of cutoff.  
• Re-estimate treating attrition as outcome; bound effects using Lee (2009) trimming.

T3. Imperfect Compliance Correlated with Outcomes  
• Fuzzy RD (2SLS within bandwidth) addresses non-compliance mechanically.  
• Report first-stage F-stats and complier profile (Angrist & Imbens 1995 diagnostics).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline

```r
# 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)     # fast data handling
library(fixest)         # fast 2SLS
library(rdrobust)       # RD estimation & plots
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load & merge ---------------------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("cps_algebra_doubledose_2003_2004.csv")   # student-level panel

# 2. Variable construction -----------------------------------------------
dt[, treat   := as.integer(double_dose == 1)]
dt[, cutoff  := as.integer(itbs_math_pct < 50)]
dt[, runvar  := itbs_math_pct - 50]                   # centered running var
# Outcomes
dt[, plan10_z   := scale(plan10_math)]               # standardize to SD=1
dt[, act11_z    := scale(act_math)]
dt[, hs_grad4   := as.integer(grad_4yrs == 1)]
dt[, college_enroll := as.integer(enroll_2yr4yr == 1)]
# Reading skill category for heterogeneity
dt[, low_read   := as.integer(itbs_read_pct < 50)]

# 3. RD sample restriction -----------------------------------------------
bw <- 10                                             # ±10 percentile points
rd <- dt[abs(runvar) <= bw & cohort %in% c(2003,2004)]

# 4. Main fuzzy RD (2SLS within bandwidth) -------------------------------
# using local linear, separate slopes:
rd[, run_neg := pmin(runvar, 0)]
rd[, run_pos := pmax(runvar, 0)]

f_rd <- feols(act11_z ~ treat | 0 | cutoff ~ run_neg + run_pos, data = rd)
summary(f_rd, stage = 1)                             # report stages

# 5. rdrobust as robustness check ----------------------------------------
rdr <- rdrobust(y = rd$act11_z, x = rd$runvar, c = 0,
                fuzzy = rd$treat, p = 1, bwselect = "mserd")
summary(rdr)

# 6. Heterogeneity by reading skills -------------------------------------
f_het <- feols(act11_z ~ treat*low_read | 0 | cutoff*low_read ~ run_neg + run_pos,
               data = rd)
summary(f_het)

# 7. Placebo outcome & covariate balance ---------------------------------
placebo <- feols(frl_status ~ treat | 0 | cutoff ~ run_neg + run_pos, data = rd)
summary(placebo)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results

Direction  
Positive effects on math course grades and standardized math scores; modest but meaningful increases in high-school graduation and college entry. Larger gains for students with weak reading skills (because the curriculum emphasized verbal explanation).

Magnitude (priors)  
• PLAN/ACT math: +0.15–0.25 SD.  
• 4-year graduation: +3–4 p.p. on a baseline of ~57 %.  
• College enrollment: +3 p.p. on a baseline of ~45 %.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)

C1: Visible jump in treatment probability at cutoff? … 1  
C2: No discontinuity in predetermined covariates? …… 1  
C3: No evidence of sorting/manipulation? ……………… 1  
C4: Robust to bandwidth/functional-form choices? …… 1  
C5: Strong first-stage (F > 10) & monotonicity? ……… 1  

Total = 5 / 5 (subject to empirical verification).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
